title: Coherence and boundary depth of the canonical finite etale pushforward algebra
statement: Let $L$ be a locally Noetherian scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions, def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and $j:U\hookrightarrow L$ an open subscheme. Suppose $\operatorname{depth}\mathcal O_{L,y}\geq2$ for every $y\notin U$ [def-weil-pbc-depth]. Let $f:X\to U$ be finite etale [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Form the actual direct image algebra $\mathcal B=(j\circ f)_*\mathcal O_X$, with its structure map induced by $f$ followed by $j$ [def-weil-pbc-comm-algebra-sheaf]. Its underlying module is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]; for every affine open $V\subseteq L$ the structure ring map $\mathcal O_L(V)\to\mathcal B(V)$ is finite; and for every $y\notin U$ the stalk $\mathcal B_y$, as a module over $\mathcal O_{L,y}$ via the stalk of the structure map, is finite and has depth at least two.

source.place: Tag 0EY6(1), depth assertion in the proof of (2); double-dual expansion and Tag 0E9I

proof.text: On an affine Noetherian open V the intersection U with V is quasi-compact. The finite etale pushforward on this intersection is finite locally free. Extend it as a finite coherent module M on V. Finite presentations commute with localization, so the double dual N of M restricts to that locally free module.

At a missing stalk with depth at least two, choose a base regular pair x,y. A finite presentation of the dual of M expresses N as a kernel between finite free modules. The first element x is injective on the kernel. If y n = x nprime in the kernel, regularity in the free source writes n = x m. Then x d(m)=0 in the free target forces d(m)=0, placing m in the kernel. This proves regularity of the pair on N when the stalk is nonzero; the zero stalk has infinite depth.

Apply the canonical Hartogs restriction isomorphism of Tag 0E9I to N. It identifies N with the actual direct image of the locally free module, hence with the underlying module of B on V. The actual direct image already carries its structure algebra map and multiplication. These identifications are canonical on overlaps. Thus the underlying module is quasi-coherent with finite affine section modules and finite stalk modules, and its boundary stalks have the asserted depth.

lean.statement:
theorem depth_two_pushforward_coherence
    {L : Scheme.{u}} [IsLocallyNoetherian L] (U : L.Opens)
    (hboundary : ∀ y : L, y ∉ U →
      (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := L.presheaf.stalk y) (L.presheaf.stalk y))
    {X : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ U.toScheme) [IsFinite f] [Etale f] :
    let g := f ≫ U.ι
    let B : L.CommAlgebraSheaf := Under.mk
      (⟨g.c⟩ : L.sheaf ⟶ (TopCat.Sheaf.pushforward CommRingCat.{u} g.base).obj X.sheaf)
    B.toModule.IsQuasicoherent ∧
      (∀ V : L.Opens, IsAffineOpen V → (B.hom.hom.app (op V)).hom.Finite) ∧
      ∀ y : L, y ∉ U →
        letI : Algebra (L.presheaf.stalk y)
            ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat y).obj B.right.obj) :=
          ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat y).map B.hom.hom).hom.toAlgebra
        ∃ hfinite : Module.Finite (L.presheaf.stalk y)
            ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat y).obj B.right.obj),
          letI := hfinite
          (2 : ℕ∞) ≤ IsLocalRing.depth (R := L.presheaf.stalk y)
            ((TopCat.Presheaf.stalkFunctor CommRingCat y).obj B.right.obj)
